title: Father's tunes and old numbers played with Bunk Johnson
summary: He recalls the tunes his father played, then old numbers and dances played with Bunk Johnson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Can you remember some of the early music you heard when you were a boy, the very first, I guess, of course, your father playing the harmonica and guitar? Well. Any bands or parades?

During that time, my father was playing. I didn't remember those numbers then because my father had been dead a long time. He died when I was ten years old. That'd make me remember none of the tunes. You wouldn't remember very much. No, but I know one tune he used to play all the time. I was small, but after the ball was over. Oh, yeah. Yeah, he played that. And another one, he used to play the old Chicken Reel. Chicken Reel.
I got the orchestration from that. Yeah. The old Robichaux band, Maurice Duran had some of Robichaux's music and he sold me a bunch of it all years ago.

Yeah, well, I remember them two old numbers good when he used to play. I was a small kid, but I remember them good. Them the two numbers even that form. No, I don't remember the others. But for the other band, I tell you, there's a lot of numbers they played. You're trying to get your work finished up. And I can't recall the NAMM back from way back. There's a lot of numbers I played with Bunk Johnson. And they were so old back. He know them all. Oh, yeah, he knew them. And right now, if he's sitting down playing, they'll come right to me. But for the NAMM of them, I couldn't call them.
You said Blue Bell's Goodbye was one I believe.
That was one of them, yeah.
I got the sheet music with that up here in the store.
Yeah. Blue Bell's Goodbye. Yeah, that was one of his numbers. I never heard of him. But Bunk's had more old numbers, I think, than any old numbers. I mean, that he kept track of.
Yeah, he could remember all of them.

He could, yeah. I never forgot of him. Yeah. I played, oh, a lot of dances with him. When we made your record, huh? We had a job to play. He played a job with us at night, yeah. And he was quite a nice fellow to be with.
Yeah, he was a good trumpet player. He remembered all of his old times. Yeah.
